title: Kilo Code operating card correction pending source verification
summary: This intermediate resource tells practitioners whether the existing operating card can be corrected safely. Product-specific instructions remain UNKNOWN and are omitted until the prior content, changed citation, and accessible first-party documentation are available.
prerequisites: The complete current contents of the existing operating-card JSON
The former cited source URL and its source entry
An accessible first-party replacement source or change notice

sections.title: Practitioner answer
paragraphs: Do not apply a product-specific correction yet. The changed citation, its former URL, its replacement URL or revised contents, its change date, and the affected claims are UNKNOWN. The existing resource contents are also unavailable, so a correction-only update cannot be distinguished from a rewrite.

Obtain the complete current JSON and the former source record first. If either is unavailable, stop and recover it from repository history or the editorial source register before editing. Then retrieve an accessible first-party replacement or change notice. If no first-party replacement can be opened over HTTPS, leave product claims unasserted and send the resource for editorial review rather than guessing.

sections.title: Change scope and procedure
paragraphs: The source recorded for review is content/resources/coding-tools/kilo-code-operating-card.json, attributed to an unregistered publisher and never verified. Whether that entry represents a moved external citation, changed source contents, or only the target file is UNKNOWN. Consequently, the claims affected by the source change are UNKNOWN and no product-specific claim or procedure is asserted here.

Compare the recovered current file with the former source and an accessible first-party replacement. If the source change cannot be dated or mapped to specific claims, record that gap and do not modify those claims. If it can be mapped, edit only the affected source entry and claims, preserving all unrelated wording, field order, and three-section structure. If a retained action lacks documented failure recovery, obtain first-party troubleshooting guidance or omit that action rather than leaving the reader stranded.

Validate the resulting file as one top-level JSON object and against the platform Resource schema. If JSON parsing fails, correct the reported syntax error and parse it again. If the platform schema or catalogue uniqueness validator is unavailable, do not claim schema or uniqueness validation; mark those checks UNKNOWN and request the authoritative validator. RFC 8259 supports the JSON syntax requirement but does not establish platform-specific fields or catalogue rules.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: A successful correction has observable evidence: repository history supplies the exact prior resource; the review record identifies the former source, replacement or revised source, change date, and affected claims; the diff changes only those claims and source entries; every retained action has a documented next step for failure; and every listed source opens directly over HTTPS.

Verify success by parsing the file as JSON, running the authoritative platform schema and catalogue checks, opening each source URL over HTTPS, and comparing the final diff with the recovered prior file. If any URL does not open, parsing or validation fails, the prior file cannot be recovered, or unrelated wording changed, the correction is not verified. Revert unrelated edits and obtain the missing evidence before publication. In the present review, current URL resolution, platform-schema conformance, catalogue uniqueness, source movement, and product-specific accuracy remain UNKNOWN because network access, the prior JSON, and the platform validator were not supplied.
